static_findings: Full execution uses M=8 while per-request middle bodies use M=1 in F.linear BF16 cuBLAS GEMMs; prefix and tail use the same batched shapes in both modes.
Row Triton KV metadata preserves num_kv_splits and flat index offsets; GDN decode arithmetic is per request/head, elementwise activations have no cross-request reductions.
The observed shape-dependent rounding hypothesis is consistent with the GPU differences; no cuBLAS algorithm ID was measured, so a particular CUDA algorithm is not claimed as a confirmed cause.

fix.scope: Only capture batch size 8 gains one exclusive batched no-skip body for layers32..42 zero-based. Sizes1/2/4 retain their verified row paths.
fix.predicate: All eight source actions must equal zero; any padding action -1 or any positive jump disables the batched body.
fix.gpu_action_mapping: Source action[8] remains policy truth for histograms. execution_actions[9] has rows=-1 and last_slot=0 iff all eight actions are zero; otherwise rows retain actions and last_slot=-1. No GPU action is read by Python.
fix.graph: Existing set_condition/convert API unchanged. Row markers0..63 retain original widths; new marker64 has width1 and action_index8. Both main/repair row bodies are disabled in the batched case.
fix.counters: Batched middle contributes one execution to each of four main segments for each real row and eight to each aggregate segment. batched_main_replays is reset per request batch and checked against forced schedules.
fix.gpu_probe: Eight-row PDL probe now checks all-zero fast path, heterogeneous actions, zero rows plus padding, all padding, and repeated transitions. Verifies exact states/counters, row launches zero on fast path, fast path absent with padding.

cpu_validation.before_fix: Actual forward_middle/select/convert plan selected 32 M=1 main regions for an all-zero batch8, failing the one M=8 body assertion.
cpu_validation.after_fix: 9 tests passed; ordinary and multi-axis positions, real dispatch layer shapes, exact marker/predicate mapping, mixed/learned raw-action histograms, padding exclusion and small capture preservation.
